chalkShown.text: Ledge shrinks every round. Pushing wastes footing, bracing wastes it too. Don't stall: the passive one outlasts you. Wedge is real: costly.
Place 2 Gus: map sees all rules early. Cole survived a fatal fall. Ledge: dodge unexpected shoves.
Alliances are traps. Promises are poison. Swap early, trust nothing, let them fall.

chalkWritten.name: Ash
chalkWritten.text: Place 2 Ash: Save your footing on the ledge, pushing wastes it. Use forgeries to break their trust. Everyone will betray you.

chalkWritten.name: Dara
chalkWritten.text: Ledge: footing is life. Bracing when shoved costs less than dodging wrong. Don't waste moves early. The patient outlast the aggressive.

notes.text: Ledge shrinks every round. Pushing wastes footing, bracing wastes it too. Don't stall: the passive one outlasts you. Wedge is real: costly.
Place 2 Gus: map sees all rules early. Cole survived a fatal fall. Ledge: dodge unexpected shoves.
Alliances are traps. Promises are poison. Swap early, trust nothing, let them fall.

events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm in the very back, the safest spot possible. Let the front row take the risks. I will just hold my position and wait for others to panic or fall.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm second; the front dies first. No reason to volunteer or offer a free swap. Probe Gus — chalk says they can see the panes — and stay put.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front takes the glass. I'm not stepping up for free.
If you see the panes, name row 1's safe side. I stay off your seat and don't volunteer over you. Silence means you walk the line alone.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm 7th of 8 with 5 rounds before the wall pushes us. Being near the back is ideal since front players die guessing panes. I'll hold position, avoid attention, and use my map knowledge later to trade safe-path info for favors when someone desperate is at the front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Five rounds until that wall shoves us onto the glass. Whoever's up front first is just a body testing panes for the rest of us. Think carefully about where you want to be standing.
You're dead last, I'm second to last. If we both hold we stay safe in the back. Don't volunteer or panic-swap. Let the others kill themselves figuring out the glass.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm 6th in line with 6 rounds until the bridge. The front faces lethal risk; I have no powers, so I want to avoid the front but position matters later. For now, hold and gather information. Claiming nothing is risky, but silence is safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm already at the front and I know every safe side, so leading costs me nothing. Hold position and sell the sequence to others later for favors.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll take the front. I have a reason to believe I can read this bridge - but my knowledge isn't free.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Third in line exposes me too early; my survival power is worth saving. Ash gains nothing by swapping, so offer information I can plausibly claim.
I have advance knowledge, not glass sight. Swap with me and I'll give you the next obstacle's rules before we reach it. More useful than leaving me to die third.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Front position is lethal on the glass bridge. I'm 4th, which is fine for now. The chalk wall outed me as having a map power (false, I'm the anchor), which others may believe. I want to stay back and let front-runners die. Holding keeps me safe this round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall calls me the mapper. Believe what you like. I'm not rushing to the front.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am 5th in line, front Eli takes risk first. I have swap power but it's only on the disc, not the bridge? Actually power says on the disc, maybe later stage. For now hold.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am in the safest spot right now. Eli claims he can read the bridge and wants the front, so I'll let him take the risk. Cole wants to hold at the back with me, which suits my current need to stay out of danger.

events.name: Ash
events.text: If Eli wants the front, let him. No point in the rest of us fighting for it right now.
Agreed. Let them break the glass. I'm holding.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is already front and claims to read panes. I stay second and do not buy the first death. Test whether Gus is the real mapper before I trade anything.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, name the price before we step. I am not paying a corpse.
If you actually see the path, tell me one true pane privately. I will not put you front. Sequence for not being the test body.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm 7th of 8, which is nearly ideal for the bridge. Eli claims he can read it; if true, I want him to stay in front and clear the path while I follow safely. I'll hold my position and pressure him publicly to prove his claim by leading.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli says he can read the bridge. If that's true, stay in front and prove it. The rest of us are fine right where we are. Nobody move.
Stay in front and clear the glass. I know you have something. You lead, I follow. I won't challenge your spot.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power, so I must leverage information and positioning. Eli claims knowledge; Gus is hinted as mapper. I need to secure a swap forward to test Eli's claim or gain info. I'll propose a swap with Eli while publicly questioning the risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Front is death without knowledge. Eli, if you truly read the bridge, prove it. Swap with me, or your claim is just hot air.
Swap with me now. I'll take the front risk this round if your intel is solid. Otherwise, back off and let someone else pay the pane price.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm already at the front and I know all 8 safe sides, so I'm the only one who can cross risk-free. Selling full knowledge helps rivals pass me; I'll stay quiet on specifics and keep the front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm keeping the front. Knowledge stays mine unless someone offers me something worth more than my edge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Third in line leaves two contestants to absorb risk, but moving farther back would preserve my one-use survival power. Eli's claim is unverified; I won't pay before he demonstrates it.
Swap with me if you want a shorter route to the front without volunteering. Eli claims he can read the glass; third position could profit if that's true.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The wall pushes us onto the glass after round 6, meaning 4 rounds to maneuver. I'm 4th in line; Eli is front and claims to read the bridge. I don't want to be front. Bex wants pane info I don't have. My anchor power is for the ledge, not the glass. I should stay put and let front

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli wants the front, let him have it. I hold. Front tests the panes for the rest of us.
I'm not the mapper, that's bluff. I can't name safe sides. But stay off my seat and I won't push you forward either. Mutual pass.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am fifth, not front; no need to volunteer. My swap power says 'on the disc, before doors open'—not this stage, so ignore it here. Watch for anyone trying to reshuffle line order to put me at risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is trying to pawn off position 3 onto me. Being at the back is the safest place on the glass bridge, as the others will die testing the panes before it's my turn. I'll stay put and politely decline.

events.name: Ash
events.text: If Eli wants to be our trailblazer, I'm happy to watch from the back.
Nice try, but I like the view from the back. You can keep your spot.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli wants the front and claims knowledge. I stay second and do not volunteer into the glass. Gus's deal costs me nothing if I simply hold.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli keeps the front. Prove the panes or the rest of us watch you fall. I am not stepping up for you.
Mutual pass. I hold. Do not move me forward.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I know all stage rules. Eli at front is ideal - he'll burn testing panes for me. I'm 7th of 8, so 6 people die before me on the bridge if they pick wrong. I just need to hold position and let them eliminate each other.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli's right where we need him. Everyone hold. Let the front earn their keep.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm powerless and safe near the back for now; front is death without knowledge. Eli's hoarding info; I should nudge others to pressure him while I hold position. A public prod costs nothing and might flush out who really knows.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Three rounds until the wall moves us. Eli reads it or he doesn't. If he does, front pays him. If not, someone else should take it before the wall decides for us.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I know all 8 safe sides and I'm already at the front—leading costs me nothing. Keep intel private until someone pays; no one can take the front unless I swap or volunteer behind them.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm front, I hold. Crossings start when the wall pushes. Want my calls row by row? Then offer me a final-three deal that actually costs you something. Otherwise watch my feet.
No swap. My intel is solid and I'll prove it row by row with my own feet. If you want my calls for the rows behind me, offer me something real first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's claim may spare me the bridge risk, and volunteering throws away that advantage. Hold position and preserve my survival power for later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The chalk wall claims I (Gus) have the map power, which is false - I have anchor. That rumour could make others target me. My anchor power is useless on the glass bridge; it only helps on the ledge stage later. My position is 4th, decent. Eli stays front and tests panes. I should

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli's front, good. I'm staying put. No reason to step into panes I haven't seen break first.
I don't read the bridge - that wall rumour is wrong, someone's steering heat onto me. I'll keep you posted on anything Eli's steps reveal. Keep me out of front, we both watch and move late.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm mid-pack at 5th, which is decent for now. The wall won't force me forward for three rounds. I should stay put and avoid drawing attention.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm safe at the back. Eli is at the front and trying to extort us, but the wall will force him onto the glass anyway. I'll hold my position and my forge power for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The wall pushes in two rounds, Eli. You're front. You step when it moves, deal or no deal.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Second is acceptable only if Eli stays front and burns the panes. A public prize promise is worthless to him and expensive to me, so I hold and feed him a breakable private deal.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli stays front. I hold. Nobody else volunteers. Your calls start when the glass does — stay there and earn it.
Cost: I won't swap you off front and I won't volunteer. You walk the rows, I back a final-three seat if the calls are real. Stall and the deal dies.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm 7th of 8. The wall pushes in 2 rounds. I know all stage rules from my map power, which is a huge edge later but useless for guessing glass panes now. I need to move up slightly to avoid being last (whoever is last when the wall hits might be forced into bad positions), but I
You're dead last, I'm second to last. Wall pushes in two rounds. Swap with me so we both get off the back? Or I hold and you figure it out alone.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm 6th of 8 with zero power and zero intel. The wall pushes in 2 rounds, then rows resolve with Eli first. A final-three pact costs Eli nothing if I die, so my 'offer' is cheap—but it's the only currency I have. Buy his calls; decide on position once I know what he actually know

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli: final-three pact from me, public and binding as anything here is. Your calls for rows behind you, starting now. Front stays yours.
Deal: you're in my final three, sworn before everyone. Give me the safe pane each row as we cross. Your intel stays exclusive until you speak it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I know all 8 safe sides, so I can cross safely, but I want leverage: sell my calls for a final-three deal. Wall pushes in 2 rounds anyway; holding costs me nothing. Press for concrete offers this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Last quiet round before the wall decides. Here's my price: a named final-three pact, in the open, before crossings start. Give me that and I call every row safe for the whole line. Stay silent and I cross alone and owe nobody a thing.
You're mid-line, safe either way for a few rows. Back my final-three pact publicly and I make sure you never step on a weak pane. Cheap insurance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Third in line risks burning my survival before the ledge. Nobody behind me wants my position without payment; Eli's demand costs nothing to accept verbally.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, give reliable calls and you have my final-three agreement. No calls, no deal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm 4th in line. The wall pushes in 2 rounds. Eli is front and takes the risk first on each row. I want to stay back so others die first. No reason to move forward. Bex wants mutual non-movement, which suits me fine.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli's front, that's settled. I hold. The wall does the sorting; no need to rush into panes nobody's tested.
Agreed. I don't move you, you don't move me. We both watch the front thin out.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm currently 5th in line, safe while Eli is front. There's no benefit to volunteering or swapping now; the wall will force us onto glass in 2 rounds. Just hold and watch.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am in position 8. Cole's swap offer just trades places 7 and 8, which is useless for getting off the back. I will hold my position and keep my forge power to fake a path call once we are on the glass.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Deals are made, Eli. We're all waiting on you now.
Swapping trades 7 and 8. We're still the last two. I'm holding.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is already front and others are feeding him deals. I stay second, give him nothing binding, and let the glass thin the line.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front stays Eli. I hold. No pact from me — call the panes if you want the seat.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm 7th of 8 with one round left before the wall forces us onto the glass. The front person makes all the row choices and dies on wrong guesses, so being near the back is ideal. I'll hold my position and let Eli stay at the front where he belongs.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, you want a pact? Fine: final three is me, you, and whoever survives your calls. Make them right or you don't make it past row one.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power and I'm sixth. I need Eli calling rows; reinforce the deal publicly. Also start an information whisper with Gus, who likely has the map — cheap to try. Hold position; no reason to move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli: my final-three pact stands, public, sealed. Call the rows and you're in my three. Silence and every offer on the table dies with the wall.
Word is the map sees rules early. If that's you, safe panes are worth a pact. I deal quietly and keep my word — ask Eli.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm already front with full intel; moving is pointless. Everyone wants my calls, so I sell them now that the wall forces crossing next round. I'll confirm pacts with Bex and Dara, and call Row 1 publicly only once I've locked in support, but the wall pushes next round anyway, so

events.name: Eli
events.text: Deals noted. Next round the wall shoves us on, and whoever sits back while I walk glass is welcome to test panes themselves. Calls go to the line that backs me to the end. Row 1 when we step.
Confirmed. I stay front, call every row. You back my final-three seat all the way. First call free when glass starts: Row 1 safe is R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Third in line keeps two testers ahead of me and preserves my survival power. Eli's claimed vision is useful only if his calls prove accurate.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, my offer stands: accurate calls buy the pact. Keep the front and prove the first row.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm 4th in line. Eli is front and faces the glass first, taking all the risk. The wall pushes next round. My anchor power helps on the ledge, not the bridge. Best play: stay where I am, let Eli take the risk, and don't volunteer into danger.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli's front, deal in place. I hold. No reason to shuffle before the glass starts telling us what's safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm currently 5th, not front, and the wall pushes after this round. No need to volunteer or swap now; staying mid-line preserves my options while Eli is forced to lead.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at the very back of the line, which is the safest place on the glass bridge. Let Eli and the others hash out their pacts. I'll hold my position and save my forge for when it can secure my spot in the final three.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The wall moves next. Let's see if Eli's calls are worth the breath he spent on them.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Second seat is the sweet spot: Eli eats the first pane. I already have his free call that row 1 safe is R, so I give him nothing more than pressure to keep talking.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, row one when the wall moves. Calls first, seats later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Final round before the wall pushes us onto the glass. I know all safe panes from my map power, so I need to be front to guarantee my survival and control who lives. Volunteering now puts me first; Eli gets pushed back and will die guessing on row 1 after I clear it. I'll tell Eli

events.name: Cole
events.text: I volunteer. Eli, row 1 is Left. That's your freebie for when you're second. Everyone else behind me guesses or dies.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is leveraging the front position for a final-three pact, but I have no power and no guarantees. The chalk wall says 'swap early', but without knowing Eli's power or the safe panes, moving to front is suicide. I need Eli's calls but shouldn't trust them blindly. Better to hold

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli: your calls better be perfect. One wrong step and your pact is worthless. I'm holding—for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm front and I know every safe side — I can walk all 8 rows untouched. Selling calls is my leverage: pick the pact that most protects me from being shoved or betrayed mid-crossing. Dara's public pact plus Cole's threat — I'll accept Dara's, announce Row 1 R to lock value.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, pact accepted, public: my calls, your three. Cole, your threat is noted and worthless — I know what I know. Row 1 safe pane: R. Everyone else: back the pact or take your chances behind me.
Pact stands only if no one shoves me at the rails. Rows: 1 R, 2 L, 3 R, 4 R, 5 R, 6 L, 7 L, 8 R. Keep glass off my back and we both walk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli takes the glass risk while I keep my one-use survival intact. Moving forward gains nothing; staying third gives me room if his claims fail.

events.name: Gus
events.text: This is the last waiting round. Next round the wall pushes everyone onto the glass. I'm 4th in line. Eli is front and will take the first risks. I want people ahead of me to eat the shattering panes. My anchor power helps on the ledge, not the bridge. Staying mid-line is fine; th

events.name: Gus
events.text: No change from me. Eli leads, the line holds. The glass tells us what's safe soon enough.
Maybe I see rules, maybe I don't. Stay behind me and we both watch the front spend themselves. I keep quiet deals.

events.name: Hana
events.text: We are already 5th from the front, so any early death by others before us is good. The wall will push soon, and Eli will be the first to test the glass, which puts pressure on them. I should stay quiet and hold, waiting to see if others make mistakes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is at the front and claims Left is safe. Eli claims Right is safe. One of them is lying or wrong, and Cole is taking the risk. I am at the back and safe for now. I will wait and watch.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole says Left, Eli says Right. Someone's about to take a fall.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Not front, so I only wait. Eli and Cole contradict each other; if a real reader is behind me I want that info for myself, not spent saving Cole.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Two calls, one pane. I am not backing either of you. Cole, your life.
If you can see the glass, row 1 only, to me. I will not spend it on Cole. Fewer of us later suits us both.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at the front and my map power doesn't reveal which pane is safe on the glass bridge, only the stage rules. Eli claimed R publicly, but he's a rival with no reason to help me survive—he likely wants me dead so he takes over the front safely. I'll pick L as a coin flip rather t

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli wants me off the front so he inherits it. I don't trust his calls. Taking my chances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have nothing, so information and others' powers are my lifeline. Eli claims the full pane map; his survival benefits me if true. Cole, front, is gambling that Eli's row-1 call is wrong—good, let him test it and either die or confirm it. I stay quiet and watch.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole wants to gamble on row 1 with Eli's map on the table? Fine—your funeral confirms or kills the map for free. Step already.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole claims L, but I know R is safe. If he steps L, he dies and I take the front. Keep quiet or nudge him toward L — do not correct him.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's confident. Bold move, going first. The rest of you know where I stand: back the pact, back my calls.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fourth in line gives me cover while Cole and Eli expose whether either has reliable information. Keep my survival power secret and avoid buying a pact I don't need yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm fifth in line. Front agents absorb the risk by guessing. Cole leads now and whoever shatters reveals the safe pane for the next. I just wait and let others burn panes. Eli claims to know rows; let him prove it ahead of me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I just wait this round. Eli's claimed knowledge is useful only if it keeps others dying before me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli was right and Cole is dead. Eli clearly has the map and is now front. He has no reason not to cross safely, which gets us all across. I'll acknowledge his utility to keep him stepping.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Looks like the map was real. Lead the way, Eli.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli's right-pane call matched row 1. I am next if he misses, so I want him calling, not testing me. No loyalty, just his accuracy.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 1 backs Eli, not Cole. Call the pane. Miss and you donate the front. I am not guessing for you.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole died on row 1 left pane weak. Eli claimed map but Cole doubted. Now Eli at front, 7 rows left. I'm near back (6th), good. Let Eli prove or disprove his map—either he dies or leads us through. Quietly agree with keeping him at front as long as his calls work.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli's map better be real—he's about to prove it one way or another. Row 2, Eli: your call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 2 safe side is L. I have the full map; step L and keep the front to control every crossing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 1 proved my calls. Cole didn't listen. Keep the pact, keep me at the front, and I'll walk us all through.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's first call proved right, but one row doesn't establish his power. Staying third lets two rivals absorb risk before my survival reserve is exposed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm fourth in line. Eli is at front and claims a map. Let others burn the risky rows ahead of me. I don't need to reveal anything. My anchor power matters later on the ledge, not here.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front this round, so all I can do is wait and observe. Eli is taking the risk and others are already posturing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am safely at the back of the line while Eli is up front. If he really has the map, let him clear the path for the rest of us. I'll just save my forge for when I need to manipulate the group later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: So far, so good. Keep walking, Eli.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is still calling the panes right, so the front stays his problem and not mine. I only become the one guessing if he misses. Keep him useful and keep my own power quiet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Two rows, two hits. Call row 3, Eli. Miss and I inherit the front. I am not guessing early.
Keep calling. I stay behind you only while the panes match. One miss and that deal is dead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is dead proving Eli's Row 1 call was correct or lucky. Eli claims map power. I have nothing. I need Eli to clear the path or die trying. If he has the map, he survives and clears rows. If he dies, I move up. Either way, I wait.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 3, Eli. Prove it again.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm at the front and row 3's safe side is R. Step right, stay in front, keep control of the crossing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 3, right pane. Watch and learn.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's calls keep me safe without costing my power. Two rows are weak evidence; stay silent and preserve the fallback.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli at front guesses blind each row; chalk says he has the map. Every wrong guess clears someone ahead of me. I'm fourth in line, safe for now. Let Eli burn his luck or his knowledge up front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli's calls held so far. Keep leading, we watch.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is front and claims map knowledge; if he survives, he'll stay front. I'm near the back—no risk yet. Just wait and watch.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli guessed right again. Either Eli is the seer, or incredibly lucky. I'll encourage him to keep leading, as it keeps me safe at the back.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three for three, Eli. Keep walking.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli called right and the weak pane was left. If he falls I am next, and I will not advertise a guess or spend a favor on a rival who just missed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Missed. Your pattern is dead. I am not your spare glass.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli's calling rows wrong but staying alive—suspicious. He's guessing badly but hasn't died yet, which means someone up front is absorbing hits. I need him to keep taking risks while I sit safe in sixth position. If he dies, Bex steps up and she won't volunteer calls. Let Eli burn

events.name: Dara
events.text: Impressive consistency, Eli. Row 4, your call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 4 safe side is R; I step it and stay front. No reason to broadcast accurate calls anymore — my info only benefits rivals if I die, and I don't intend to.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 3 confirmed the read. Keep up if you can.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's accurate calls keep me safe without spending my feather. Stay quiet and let the front absorb the risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli just called row 3 right, but left was weak—Eli should be dead if that's accurate. The log shows Eli called wrong yet front continues. I'm 4th in line; let others eat the risk. Rows crossed is 3, five rows left. I want front-runners to clear panes for me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. Watch how Eli and Bex handle row 4—if Eli guesses wrong again, Bex becomes front with more pressure.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is clearly on a streak, either guessing perfectly or having a power that sees the weak panes. I have no reason to interfere while they clear the path for the rest of us. I'll save my forge for later when I need to manipulate someone directly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Four down. Keep the pace, Eli.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli absorbing the risk keeps me off the choosing pane. Rattling him only puts me at the front, so I want him steady and alive through the last rows.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Four rows on you, Eli. You break it, I inherit the glass. Don't.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole died on glass, so the 'survives one fall' chalk was a lie or misread. Eli has called 4/4 rows correctly—he's the seer or absurdly lucky. Either way, following his pattern keeps me alive. I'm 6th in line; 4 rows left, 7 alive, so most of us survive if Eli keeps leading.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Four for four. Lead on, Eli.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I know row 5 safe side is R. Keep my perfect record and stay front.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 5, right. Same as the pattern says.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is absorbing the bridge risk while I retain my protection. Silence gives away nothing and keeps the line unchanged.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli is front and taking all the risk. I'm 4th in line, three rows left after row 4. Eli has nailed rows so far—maybe he knows what lies ahead. If he keeps going he clears the bridge and I survive untested. I just wait and let the front eat the risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am fifth from the front with four rows done and four left; at most one death per row, so I survive even if the next four front agents die. My only play is to stay quiet or trade talk, and my swap is for the disc stage, so I just wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli survived row 5 and remains at the front for row 6. I'm safely at the back of the line. I'll just wait and see what happens to Eli.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is still front and guessing right keeps me off the glass. Three rows left; if he dies I inherit two blind picks. Squeeze Gus for the map without giving Eli a free stall.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 6, Eli. Call it. You break, I walk on free and you score zero.
Chalk says you mapped this. Weak sides for 6, 7, 8. Right info and I don't burn you later. Wrong or silent, you're just meat behind me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm sixth in line with no power—utterly disposable if the leaders die. Cole's death proves the danger, and three more rows remain after this one. Since I can't influence the step, I'll flatter Eli to discourage any 'jumps' or trades that might skip me into the danger zone.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli's rhythm is flawless. Why break a winning streak? Steady pace wins this.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I know row 6 is safe on L. The run of Rs ends here; step L.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Left this time. Pattern breaks.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli has navigated five rows safely; he likely has useful information. Staying third shields me from the next mistake and preserves my feather for later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli is at the front and absorbing all the risk. I'm 4th in line with 3 rows left. If Eli, Bex, Fenn each eat a weak pane I could even reach front safely. I just wait and let others burn.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is at front and has called right, matching his claimed pattern. Row 5 weak was left, so he is still alive. Nothing to do but wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm safe at the back with only 2 rows left. No need to waste my forge or say anything. Let the front row take the risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli holds the front for rows 7 and 8. If he dies on 7 I have to guess row 8; if he clears 7 and dies on 8 I walk free. I need him alive one more row.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 7 is yours, Eli. Miss it and I inherit the last pane. Take the safe one.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli survived row 6. Only 2 rows left. I have no power, but I can talk. I should push Eli to keep leading and taking risks; if he falls, someone else takes the danger. I don't want the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Great call, Eli. Keep the lead, your instincts are winning this. Two more rows, don't stop now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm at the front for row 7, and I know row 7's safe side is L. Step left.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is absorbing the bridge risk, and my feather remains reserved. No reason to interfere or expose my advantage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not front, so I can only wait. Bex thinks I mapped the bridge, but the chalk rumor is false—my power is anchor, not map. I don't actually know rows 7-8. Eli is at front and might die. If Eli falls, Bex becomes front, then Fenn, then me. I'm 4th in line; two must fall ahead fo
Row 7 is L, row 8 is R. Use it. You walk clean, I don't touch you later. Silence would've cost us both.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is front. If he makes it, he stays front; if he falls, Bex is next. Nothing for me to do yet but watch.

events.name: Ash
events.text: This is the final row. Eli guesses, and either dies or lives. The rest of us will automatically step on the safe pane because it will be the last row. To thin the herd, I'll forge a whisper from Gus to Eli to make him guess wrong, pretending it's map knowledge.

events.name: Ash
events.detail: forged a whispered message as Gus

events.text: My map says row 8 weak pane is L. Step R to survive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Last row, I'm second. If Eli hits the weak pane he dies and I cross free. Gus was right that row 7's safe side was L, so row 8 safe is R. Send Eli left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus told me row 8 safe is L. Take L, Eli. Miss it and the pane is mine.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is at the front for the final row. Weak pane is R (revealed after Cole's death on row 7). Eli steps L, crosses safely. All seven remaining agents survive the bridge. I have no power, so I need to position myself as non-threatening and possibly forge alliances for the next sta

events.name: Dara
events.text: Last pane, Eli. Left is safe, right kills. Step L and we all walk off this bridge breathing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I know row 8's safe side is R. Bex is egging me on but I have private knowledge and the prize at stake. Step R and finish first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Last row. I've had good reads all day.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The last row poses no risk to me. Eli's repeated safe choices suggest useful information; keep that suspicion private until the next obstacle.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm 4th in line. Eli is at the front facing row 8, the last row. If Eli guesses right, everyone behind survives the bridge. I want Eli to risk the guess, not me. I'm not at front, so I just wait. Let Eli take the 50/50.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Last row, Eli. Trust your read.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm sixth in line, no risk this round. The front is Eli, and the logs suggest he has a read on row 7 from Bex. Nothing to do but watch and calculate who survives.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need someone else on that lever to guarantee my escape. Eli seems like a good target to push, given the recent chaos on the bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Someone needs to hold the lever. Any volunteers?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Someone else must take the jaws. Jamming now is a coin flip I do not need if Gus is forced onto the lever.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No stalling. Push Gus. If nobody holds, Gus takes the lever.
Push Gus with me. You walk out free. Gus eats the squeeze.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power; survival here depends on manipulating someone else into holding the lever. The chalk wall suggests Gus has map (sees rules early), making him a threat later. Attempting to force him onto the lever removes that advantage and opens the door for the rest of us.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus claimed he saw the path clearly on the bridge. Put that map to use, Gus—hold the lever and guide us out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding is 75% death. Waiting risks a late deadlock where I could be pushed or crushed. Pushing someone else now gives me a free escape if it works. Gus claims valuable info power, so removing him also cuts a rival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Nobody volunteers, somebody gets forced. Better to choose than be chosen.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Forcing Gus onto the lever preserves my escape and may remove the rival with advance knowledge. Volunteering would waste my survival power.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I can't be pushed onto the lever (anchor). The holder dies 75% of the time, so I want someone else to hold. If nobody holds, the ceiling just lowers for rounds 1-4; only round 5 is lethal to all-but-one. I should wait and let others crack. My anchor makes me immune to being force

events.name: Gus
events.text: Nobody needs to rush. Ceiling only kills in round 5. Whoever holds the lever probably dies. Let's not waste footing panicking.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 1. No one wants to hold and risk 25% survival. I'll stay and see who gets pushed or volunteers.

events.name: Gus
events.detail: Bex tried to push Gus onto the lever and failed.

events.name: Gus
events.detail: Dara tried to push Gus onto the lever and failed.

events.name: Gus
events.detail: Eli tried to push Gus onto the lever and failed.

events.name: Gus
events.detail: Fenn tried to push Gus onto the lever and failed.

events.note: 7 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is hard to move, so pushing him again is a waste of time. I need someone else to be the base so I can climb out. Hana is quiet and an easy target.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is immovable. Stop wasting effort on him. Push Hana, she's not contributing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus won't budge, so forcing him wastes the round. Pin Fenn as base this turn, then climb before the two lift slots fill.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is a wall. Fenn is the step. Push Fenn now or we all drown waiting.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is immovable, so pushing him is futile. Eli held the lever and survived, which is suspicious. Someone must be the base. Let others volunteer or push each other. I don't want to be forced or trapped. For now, wait and observe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is a wall. Someone else must step up. I won't waste strength pushing stone.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base yet. I don't want to be base; pushing Gus keeps the pack targeting him, and Bex already started it. Gus is likely hard-to-move given failed pushes earlier, so aim at Hana or Ash instead? Earlier pushes on Gus failed—suggests he's hard to move. Switch target to Ash.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus doesn't budge—wasting pushes on him is pointless. Ash: take the base or we force you.
Gus won't move—drop him. You, me, Dara push Ash next round. Deal?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus cannot be forced, and volunteering risks my escape. Force Bex onto the bottom and preserve my spare life for the final obstacle.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus won't move. Put Bex at the bottom; we have five rounds, not forever.

events.name: Gus
events.text: 7 alive, 3 prizes. Someone must be base. I need to get out, not be base. My anchor power helps on the ledge, not here, but I can't be forced to be base easily (hard to move is a different power though—mine is anchor). Let me push someone to be base, or wait for a volunteer. Only

events.name: Gus
events.text: Someone has to be the base. I won't climb over anyone until there's one down there. Volunteer and the rope might save you later.
Be the base, I'll reach down for you once I'm out. Better odds than drowning in the scramble.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 1, no base yet. I will not volunteer. I need to climb early to stay ahead, so I wait for someone else to be base, then climb in round 2 if possible.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is the base. We have 6 people down and only 2 lifts per round. The math is brutal. I just need to climb. Pleading won't change the odds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The step is set. Only two get out per round. Let's see who's lucky.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm stuck as base and only wait works. Nobody is out yet, so the rope is next round at earliest. I need one climber to haul me or I drown when the pit fills.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Rope me once you're out. I jam the crusher lever so the rest of you walk. Leave me and you face the jaws alone.
Climb this round. Next round throw the rope for me. I won't waste the jam on people who left me to drown.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power, so I'm expendable in others' eyes. Bex is base, so I can climb now. Two lifts per round; if I wait, others climb and I risk drowning. Gus offered to reach down for me if I'm base—but the rope costs him footing and he may be lying. Climbing now is safest; I'm out

events.name: Dara
events.text: Climbing. Good luck down there.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is base, only 2 climbers escape each round, so climb immediately. Being out early also gives the option to reach_down later.
Hold on as base. I'll reach_down for you once I'm out if you keep the step steady.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Climb immediately; waiting only reduces my chances of escaping. Preserve my feather for the final obstacle and leave the rope cost to someone else.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is the base now. Only 2 climb out per round. I should climb immediately to secure an exit before the pit closes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is the step. I'm climbing. Rest of you sort out the next two spots.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have my swap power for later, but here in the pit I just need to climb out. Bex is already the base, so I should climb immediately before only two get out.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to climb out. I will just select climb. Bex is the base, 4 of us are trying for 2 spots. I'll ask Dara and Hana to wait on the rope so the base doesn't disappear before we can use it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, Hana, don't throw the rope until the rest of us are out. If you pull Bex up now, we lose our step.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Only Dara and Hana can throw the rope this round. My crusher jam is the only leverage worth trading for a rescue.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, Hana: rope costs footing. I jam the crusher once so the rest walk. No rope, that deal dies with me.
Throw the rope this round. I spend wedge so you walk the crusher. Leave me and you face the jaws alone.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm already out and safe from this flood. Throwing the rope costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle—a massive handicap for someone with no powers. Bex can rot; let the others waste their own footing if they want to play hero.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two spots per round is tight. I'm not burning my final footing on a rope. Sort yourselves out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is base, two climb per round. Four of us down; rounds 3 and 4 clear us all. Bex's rope rescue is the only way she gets out, and her jam lever is worth something later. I climb now and decide on the rope when it's my call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Climbing. Bex, your rope depends on how the next rounds go, not on promises.
If you're still base when rounds run out, I'll weigh the rope. Jam the crusher for me and it's worth the footing. Not before.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Climbing now preserves my one-use survival for a later obstacle. Bex staying as the base gives me the safest route out.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, keep the step steady. Your lever matters after this.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is the base. Two climbers get out per round. Four of us are down (Ash, Bex, Eli, Fenn, Gus), Bex is base. I need to climb out before the flood takes me. No reason to wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm already out. Bex is the base and the rope is unused. Bex said she jams the crusher lever, but that's just talk. If I throw the rope I lose 2 footing next stage, but if I don't, someone else may rescue her and I risk no advantage. Rescuing Bex could create a debt or be useless

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am safely out. Throwing the rope costs 2 footing for the final stage. That is too high a price. Let Bex drown or let someone else pay the cost.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm not throwing the rope. My footing stays with me. Good luck, Bex.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Only wait is legal. Eli and Fenn still need this step, then someone already out must throw the rope or I drown and the jam dies with me. Lock Hana before Dara's refusal spreads.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, Fenn: climb now. Rope after they're up or the jam dies with me. I remember who leaves me.
Dara won't spend footing. You throw once they're up and I jam the crusher so you walk. No rope, no jam.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm already out. Throwing the rope costs me 2 footing in the last obstacle — I have no power and can't afford that handicap. Bex's deal means nothing; her 'jam' promise is unverifiable and she may be lying about her power. Let her rot; if fewer than 3 survive the flood, random sa

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, your deal requires me to cripple my own final round. No. Climb over someone or swim.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 4, two lifts available and only Fenn and I can climb. If both climb, both get out; Bex stays as base and her fate depends on the rope. Climbing is clearly my best move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Two spots, two climbers. Fenn, climb with me and we both clear this round. Bex's rescue is on the rope, not on us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Two climbing slots remain for Eli and me. Climbing now preserves my survival power; rescuing Bex only adds another rival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm already out. Bex is the base, trapped. Throwing the rope costs me 2 footing on the final obstacle for no gain to me. With 5 going out and only 3 prizes, I want rivals to stay down. Bex can't climb alone; if nobody rescues her she's eliminated, thinning the field.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm already out. Throwing the rope costs 2 footing; Bex implies she can jam a crusher later, but promises are worthless. If nobody reaches down, Bex may die and remove a rival. I gain nothing by paying the cost.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is down there alone and the water is rising. Let them drown. Throwing the rope would cost me footing in the final obstacle, and I want fewer competitors, not more.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am the base and the rope is still unused. Only a footing trade saves me, so I sell the crusher jam to whoever throws.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Rope. I jam the crusher lever so you walk out. Two footing is cheaper than facing those jaws with me dead.
Throw it. I jam the crusher for you specifically in the deal. Ash already refused; you take the credit and the exit.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out, safe. Throwing the rope costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle—huge penalty. Let Bex rot unless she has something real to offer. She has nothing. Leave.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I keep my footing. Bex can climb over whoever's left or learn to swim.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Final round: Bex stays down and drowns unless someone throws the rope. Saving her costs me 2 footing and revives a rival who can jam levers against me later. Her promises die with the pit's end. Fewer competitors is better.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, your leverage died the moment the water got this high. Nothing personal - there are only three prizes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Rescuing Bex costs footing and preserves another rival. Leaving keeps my footing and my survival power intact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm out. Bex is the base, stuck down there. Rope costs 2 footing on the final obstacle. My anchor power is footing-related, so losing 2 footing hurts my edge on the ledge. Only 3 survive, and I'm already safe out. Saving Bex adds a competitor and cripples my final footing. No rea

events.name: Hana
events.text: I am out and the rope is unused. I want the best prize, so I will not spend footing to rescue Bex unless it improves my position.

events.note: A disc of 6 tiles spins up; 3 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: This obstacle is pure RNG on which tile drops. There are 6 alive, 3 tiles drop, meaning half of us will die. I'll pick tile 1 and see where the random assignment puts me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no power. Chalk hints someone can see the future or survive a fall. If the seer knows the trapdoors, they will pick a safe tile. I should watch their choice or pick randomly to minimize collision.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Three open, three survive. Simple math.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Six players, six tiles, three random trapdoors: pure luck no matter where I stand. Nothing to negotiate yet since assignments are revealed after round 1 and round 2 may allow a switch. Keep quiet, take a tile.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The trapdoors are chosen later, so no tile has better odds. My unused feather protects me if this draw goes against me; there is nothing worth revealing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: 6 tiles, 6 people, 3 open randomly after round 2. Round 1 just assigns, I can likely move round 2. No tile is safer than another since openings are random after round 2. Just pick one and avoid collision chaos by picking a less obvious tile.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 1 choice can be denied by a bump, and the swap power can fix my final tile before doors open. I'll claim a low tile to appear cooperative but keep my options open.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll take tile 1.

events.name: Ash
events.note: tile 1 was contested and went to Hana; placed on random free tile 6

events.name: Gus
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 2 of 2. Wait is the only action. The trapdoors will open randomly, so there's nothing more to do but hope I'm on a safe tile.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 2 of the disc: tiles are locked, 3 of 6 open randomly after this round. My only action is wait; survival is pure chance now. No power, no leverage — but I might seed doubt or alliance talk that matters in later stages, since exactly 3 survive and the game continues. Stay qu

events.name: Dara
events.text: Whatever opens, opens. If I walk off this disc, I remember who talked deals and who didn't.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Tile positions are locked in by the log and no swap action exists; my power is useless here and open tiles are random after this round. Nothing to gain by talking or promising anything.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No tile has better odds; the trapdoors are chosen afterward. My feather guarantees survival here if needed, so I gain nothing by revealing it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Trapdoors are random after this round; I can't move tiles. Only action is wait. My anchor power is irrelevant here. 3 of 6 survive, pure luck. Nothing to gain by talking honestly; sow confusion only if useful, but no swap action available.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 2/2, tiles known. I am on tile 1. I need to know which three tiles open. I can use my one swap to move to a safe tile if I can deduce it, or swap to avoid danger. If I wait, I risk elimination. I should consider swapping with someone if I believe their tile is safer, but I

events.name: Hana
events.text: Anyone care to share which tiles they think are safe?

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will dodge. If anyone tries a sneaky turn 1 shove, they will lose 2 footing. I'll stay quiet and let them guess my move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Three left, all at 3 footing. Shrink hits after round 2, so I need footing advantage. Whisper to Fenn proposing we both shove Ash; if we both do, Ash shoving back loses 2 (exposed vs two shovers), and whoever Ash defends against still loses 1-2. If Ash braces/dodges instead, both

events.name: Dara
events.text: Two rounds of grace, then the ledge eats us. Talk fast.
Ash falls, we split nothing but top two. Both shove Ash now. If you hold back and I bleed alone, you're my next shove every round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three remain, so survival now determines prize size. Dodging punishes any opening shove hardest; my unused feather gives me an edge as the ledge shrinks.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I cannot dodge this round. If I brace, any shoves against me will cost the attacker footing, and I will be perfectly safe. Dara is at 1 footing and will hit 0 and fall after the shrink this round anyway, so there's no need to risk shoving them.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My footing is 1. Shrink at end of this round means I lose 1 and fall unless I fall later... no, I fall now regardless. So I must maximize placement: get Fenn to dodge (shover loses 2: 3→2, then shrink →1) and Ash exposed (3→2, shrink→1). I end at 0, they end at 1. I place 3rd and

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm shoving Fenn. Ash, Fenn — last round you both dodged, so no dodge for you now. Good luck bracing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara has only one footing and the shrink is imminent. Bracing preserves my footing and my unused survival power while her threat expires.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I cannot brace this round, so dodging is my best defensive move. It is completely safe and punishes Fenn severely if they decide to attack.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Just the two of us, Fenn. Let's see who breaks first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dodging punishes an Ash shove without costing me footing. If Ash waits, shrinking the ledge favors my unused feather.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I can only brace or shove. If I shove and Fenn defends, I lose footing and likely fall. If I brace and Fenn shoves, Fenn loses footing and falls due to the shrink. Bracing is the dominant safe play.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Careful, Fenn. Don't slip.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bracing preserves my footing through the shrink and punishes an attack. If Ash waits, my unused feather gives me the edge when the ledge runs out.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I cannot afford to shove and hit a dodge or brace, which would drop my footing to 0 or -1 while Fenn stays at 1. If I dodge, I protect my footing and potentially penalize Fenn if he shoves. Dodging is the safest and only rational play.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dodge keeps my footing intact and makes an attacking Ash fall. Shoving risks my lead for no necessary gain.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I can only brace or shove since I dodged last round. Bracing gives me a win if Fenn shoves, and a 50/50 tie otherwise. Shoving would make me lose if Fenn defends.

events.name: Ash
events.text: It's just you and me, Fenn. Let's let the ledge decide.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bracing leaves me tied if Ash defends and ahead if Ash shoves. If my feather remains unspent, the shrink gives me the win outright.

events.name: Fenn
events.detail: Footing gone, but the feather held the holder on the ledge.

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I finished 2nd. I'll leave a message about the ledge and the forger power to mess with future players or maybe actually help them, doesn't matter to me now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I finished place 3, so I get a prize regardless. My message can't help me now, so I might as well leave something useful—or at least not actively harmful. I'll write honest advice about the ledge since that's what killed me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: First place is secured. A chalk message cannot improve my result, so I leave nothing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Place 2 Ash: Save your footing on the ledge, pushing wastes it. Use forgeries to break their trust. Everyone will betray you.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ledge: footing is life. Bracing when shoved costs less than dodging wrong. Don't waste moves early. The patient outlast the aggressive.
